Create a coverage badge

Source: R/badge.R
badge.Rd

Write an SVG badge showing the percent coverage, in the style of the badges made by Codecov and shields.io, so a README can show the coverage of a package without uploading it to a coverage service. The badge is made locally and doesn't need a network connection.

Usage

badge(x, file = "coverage.svg", label = "coverage")

Arguments

x

the coverage object returned from package_coverage()

file

the name of the SVG file

label

the text on the left side of the badge

Value

The lines of the SVG file, invisibly, after writing them to file.

Details

The coverage is that of percent_coverage(), rounded down to a whole percent so that only fully covered code shows 100%. The badge is green for coverage of 90% or more, yellow for 75% or more and red below that, the same thresholds used by report(). Coverage without any lines of code, such as that of a package with no R code, shows as unknown on a gray badge.

The badge is a plain file, so on a continuous integration service it needs to be stored somewhere that the README can link to, e.g. committed to a separate branch of the repository. system.file("workflows", "test-coverage-badge.yaml", package = "covr") is a GitHub Actions workflow that does this.

Examples

cov <- code_coverage(
  "f <- function(x) {\n  y <- x + 1\n  if (y > 0) {\n    'yes'\n  } else {\n    'no'\n  }\n}",
  "f(1)"
)
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".svg")
badge(cov, tmp)
cat(readLines(tmp), sep = "\n")
#> <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="97" height="20" role="img" aria-label="coverage: 75%">
